sheets.name: README
rows: Traceability view for one regulation-to-SHACL generation run.
Generation is frozen before RDF execution; no ship graph or hidden expected outcome is used here.
events.jsonl is append-only; CSV and Excel sheets are derived views.
Static validation passed and the semantic validator accepted the candidate.
No verified canonical term was available; the generator was not allowed to invent one.
Accepted shapes await the separate bulk evaluator.

sheets.name: RUNS
rows: The candidate faithfully encodes the direct-static conditional requirement: it targets ships, enforces the shipCategory range, uses the correct A/B, oil-tanker, deadweight < 5000 metric-tonne, and construction-date applicability conditions, requires both protection statuses when applicable, and provides explicit SHACL Core alternatives for each non-applicable condition. Datatypes, thresholds, units, namespace, ownership, and prior repair instructions are preserved.

sheets.name: ITERATIONS
rows: The conditional applicability is too restrictive and can create an accidental pass: it requires both shipType = "oil_tanker" and an additional rdf:type nltl:oilTanker assertion, although the verified condition is the single ship_type = oil_tanker criterion. Do not make equivalent oil-tanker representations conjunctively mandatory; use the authoritative representation or an explicit equivalent alternative. Also enforce the declared shipCategory range (nltl:polarShipCategoryValue), rather than only sh:nodeKind sh:IRI. Preserve the strict category A/B, deadweight < 5000, and construction date >= 2017 applicability and require both protection statuses to be true when applicable.

Replace the four combinatorial SPARQL constraints used to express non-applicability with SHACL Core alternatives: retain one applicable branch requiring category A/B, shipType oil_tanker, deadweight < 5000 tonnes, constructionDate >= 2017-01-01, and both protection statuses true, plus Core-only branches for each failed prerequisite. Preserve the canonical shipCategory range and the existing datatypes and metric-tonne unit; do not add an applicability boolean or require the absent oilTanker class representation.

The candidate faithfully encodes the direct-static conditional requirement: it targets ships, enforces the shipCategory range, uses the correct A/B, oil-tanker, deadweight < 5000 metric-tonne, and construction-date applicability conditions, requires both protection statuses when applicable, and provides explicit SHACL Core alternatives for each non-applicable condition. Datatypes, thresholds, units, namespace, ownership, and prior repair instructions are preserved.
